newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U says incontinence drug has key potential.
newsitem.headline: P&U says incontinence drug has key potential.

text.p: Swedish-U.S. drug company Pharmacia & Upjohn's incontinence drug Detrusitol has the potential to become the company's largest product, the head of P&U's research and development division said.

"Without a doubt it has the potential to become our biggest product...If we do things right it should become the biggest," Goran Ando, head of the company's Swedish operations, or PPC Sweden, told Reuters in an interview.
P&U's largest drug is currently growth hormone Genotropin which has sales of about three billion crowns annually.
P&U said last week it had applied to register the drug with Swedish authorities and estimates it will do the same with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in the first quarter of 1997.
He could not give a sales estimate for Detrusitol, or similar drug Tolterodine, but said urinary incontinence was a common problem.
"Around a third of the world's population suffer from urinary incontinence," he said.
Results of clinical studies have been positive, he said.
"What we have seen is that it is clearly an effective substance. Many patients have moved from illness to a healthy or considerably better life," said Ando.
The side effects are not as bad as for drugs now on the market, he said.
"The side effects picture is significantly better than for existing drugs," he said.
Ando declined to say when the company expected drug authority approval in Sweden, which acts as a reference country for wider approval in the European Union.
"But we understand that the Swedish drug approval authority are satisfied that we have submitted our crown jewel to them," he said.
